simple.meaning: שָׁלַב (shâlab) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to space off; intensive ( evenly ) to make equi-distant.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Exodus, beginning at Exodus 26:17. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁלַב (H7947) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שָׁלַב (shâlab) / H7947 is traced through Exodus 26:17, Exodus 36:22 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to space off; intensive ( evenly ) to make equi-distant
definitions.full: H7947. shalab [ שָׁלַב ] verb Pu`al be bound, joined (Late Hebrew Punic = Biblical Hebrew; שְׁלִיבָה rung of ladder; Aramaic שְׁלִיבִין apparently only 1Kin 7:28-29 , , ravine, narrow path between mountains ; Arabic is seize, carry off, by force ); — Participle feminine plural מְשֻׁלָּבֹת Exod 26:17 tenons joined each to ( אֶל ) its fellow, 36:22 (both P).

occurrences.englishText: There shall be two tenons in each board, joined to one another: thus you shall make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
Each board had two tenons, joined to one another. He made all the boards of the tabernacle this way.
